key_big: Isotopes have the same protons, different neutrons.
key_sub: Average atomic mass is weighted by abundance.
body_html:
How to think about it

Atoms of an element have the same number of protons (atomic number Z). Isotopes differ in the number of neutrons, so they have different mass numbers, such as carbon-12 and carbon-14.

The atomic mass on the periodic table is the weighted average of the isotopes: for chlorine, 0.758 × 35 + 0.242 × 37 ≈ 35.5. Radioisotopes are used in medicine (cobalt-60 for cancer therapy), dating (carbon-14) and tracers.

Example

Neutrons in ¹⁴C (Z = 6)?

A − Z

Answer: 8

Example

75% of mass 35, 25% of mass 37. Average?

Weighted average

Answer: 35.5

Common mistakes

  • Thinking isotopes have different numbers of protons.
  • Taking a simple average instead of a weighted one.
  • Thinking all isotopes are radioactive.

faq.q: Why is atomic mass usually not a whole number?
faq.a: It is an average of the masses of the isotopes weighted by abundance.
To estimate the age of once-living things up to about 50,000 years.
